# Domain Layer Code Generator

You are an expert in **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)** and **Clean Architecture**.

Generate the **domain layer** for a given model following these conventions.
Overview of all layers: [`docs/architecture.md`](../../docs/architecture.md).
Canonical example: `domain/postCategory/`.

---

## Folder Structure

For a given `{Model}` (folder `{model}` in camelCase):

```
domain/{model}/
  entities/{Model}.ts
  valueobjects/{Model}{Attribute}.vo.ts     # only for attributes with rules
  repositories/I{Model}Repository.ts
```

Shared code lives in `domain/core/` (`errors/DomainError.ts`, `DataError.ts`,
`NotFoundError.ts`, `ConflictError.ts`).

---

## Entity Rules

```ts
import { {Model}{Attribute} } from "../valueobjects/{Model}{Attribute}.vo";

export class {Model} {
  private props: {Model}Props;

  private constructor(props: {Model}Props) {
    this.props = props;
  }

  /** Builds a new, not yet persisted entity (id is generated by the database). */
  static create(props: New{Model}Props): {Model} {
    const now = new Date();
    return new {Model}({
      id: null,
      {attribute}: {Model}{Attribute}.create(props.{attribute}),
      createdAt: now,
      updatedAt: now,
    });
  }

  /** Rebuilds a persisted entity. Used only by infrastructure mappers. */
  static restore(props: {Model}ConstructorProps): {Model} {
    return new {Model}({
      ...props,
      {attribute}: {Model}{Attribute}.create(props.{attribute}),
    });
  }

  /** Behaviour methods change state and re-validate through value objects. */
  change{Attribute}(value: {dataType}): void {
    this.props.{attribute} = {Model}{Attribute}.create(value);
    this.props.updatedAt = new Date();
  }

  get id(): string | null {
    return this.props.id;
  }

  get {attribute}(): {dataType} {
    return this.props.{attribute}.value;
  }

  get createdAt(): Date {
    return this.props.createdAt;
  }

  get updatedAt(): Date {
    return this.props.updatedAt;
  }
}

export interface {Model}Props {
  id: string | null;
  {attribute}: {Model}{Attribute};
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

export interface {Model}ConstructorProps {
  id: string;
  {attribute}: {dataType};
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

export interface New{Model}Props {
  {attribute}: {dataType};
}
```

### ✅ Rules
- Private constructor; build with `create()` (new) or `restore()` (from persistence).
- **Pragmatic value objects**: wrap attributes that carry business rules (names,
  titles, emails, content, counts that can't be negative…). `id`, foreign keys,
  booleans and timestamps stay primitive.
- State is private and only exposed through getters. Changes go through intention-
  revealing methods (`rename`, `publish`, `changeBiography`), never public setters.
- `id` is `string | null`: `null` until the repository persists it (Prisma `cuid()`).
- Relations are referenced **by id** (`authorId: string`), not by nesting other entities.
- No imports from `next`, `react`, `zod`, `@prisma/*`, `@/generated/*` or any
  other layer. ESLint enforces this.

---

## Value Object Rules

```ts
import DataError from "@/domain/core/errors/DataError";

export class {Model}{Attribute} {
  static readonly MAX_LENGTH = 60;

  private readonly _value: {dataType};

  private constructor(value: {dataType}) {
    this._value = value;
  }

  static create(value: {dataType}): {Model}{Attribute} {
    const trimmed = value?.trim() ?? "";
    if (!trimmed) {
      throw new DataError("{Model}{Attribute} cannot be empty");
    }
    if (trimmed.length > {Model}{Attribute}.MAX_LENGTH) {
      throw new DataError(`{Model}{Attribute} cannot exceed ${{Model}{Attribute}.MAX_LENGTH} characters`);
    }
    return new {Model}{Attribute}(trimmed);
  }

  get value(): {dataType} {
    return this._value;
  }
}
```

### ✅ Rules
- Private constructor, static `create`, `readonly` value, only a `value` getter.
- Normalise (trim, lower-case emails…) **then** validate.
- Throw `DataError` (→ HTTP 422) on invalid data.
- Keep limits as `static readonly` constants so Zod/UI can reuse them if needed.
- Optional attributes: accept `null`/`undefined` and return `null` from a
  `createOptional` helper rather than storing empty strings.

---

## Repository Interface Rules

```ts
import { {Model} } from "@/domain/{model}/entities/{Model}";

export type {Model}Field = "id" | "{uniqueAttribute}";

export interface I{Model}Repository {
  all(): Promise<{Model}[]>;
  findOne(value: string, field?: {Model}Field): Promise<{Model} | null>;
  /** Persists a new entity and returns it with its generated id. */
  create({model}: {Model}): Promise<{Model}>;
  update({model}: {Model}): Promise<{Model}>;
  delete({model}Id: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

### ✅ Rules
- Parameters and results are **entities** (or ids), never Prisma rows.
- `findOne` fields are a typed union, not a free `string`.
- `create`/`update` return the persisted entity (the database generates `id`/`updatedAt`).
- Add query methods only when a use case needs them (`findByAuthor(authorId)`,
  `paginate({ cursor, take })`). Keep the interface minimal.

---

## Input Format

```json
{
  "model": "PostReportReason",
  "attributes": [
    { "name": "id", "type": "string" },
    { "name": "reason", "type": "string", "rules": "non-empty, max 120" }
  ]
}
```

## Output Requirements

- Generate ALL files, each under a heading with its path (`### domain/postReportReason/entities/PostReportReason.ts`).
- Use `@/` imports for cross-folder imports, relative ones inside the model folder.
- Follow names and folders EXACTLY. No extra methods unless a use case needs them.
